reason: Confirmed in-scope claim c3: for FP16-representable values immediately adjacent to the 2.414213562373095 interval threshold (all legal inputs per problem.txt, which explicitly declares every finite FP16 value legal and requires abs(actual[i]-atan(x[i])) <= 1e-6 with rel tol 0 as a single domain-wide verdict), the probe found 17 of 34 boundary-adjacent values violating the tolerance, max error 3.29e-6 at x=2.4140625 — more than 3x the allowed absolute error. This is not a rounding-order or declared-format artifact; the contract fixes a strict absolute tolerance on the exact stored FP16 value, and the FP32 rational approximation demonstrably fails it at the interval seam. No test.py/get_inputs narrow the domain, so problem.txt is the operative contract. c1 (mid interval) is rebutted by an exhaustive sweep (max 6.01e-7, no violations) and c2 (large magnitudes/extrema) is rebutted (error at 65504 is 5.1e-8; the small-value violations in that probe's output came from inputs outside c2's scope, consistent with the seam failure already captured in c3). Skeptic reviewed all evidence and recorded no new claims.
